Last Friday (the 21st), in the verdict of the Hong Kong Alliance case, during the early morning hours, police escorted a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle and took her away. In response to inquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of having something slightly seditious about her clothing," and took her onto a police vehicle and left. While the officers were taking the woman away, several officers continuously instructed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and pulled the orange cordon line toward the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "court-watching enthusiast" who was queuing near the woman said that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

"集誌社" inquired with the police as to the reason the woman was taken away and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation conducted in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
